html:
In 1169 Norman knights from Wales landed in southeast Ireland, invited by Diarmait Mac Murchada, the exiled King of Leinster. Within two years they held Dublin and much of the east.

Their leader, Richard de Clare, known as Strongbow, married Diarmait's daughter and became his heir. King Henry II of England, afraid of an independent Norman kingdom, crossed to Ireland in 1171 and received the submission of the Normans and of many Irish kings. The pope had given his blessing.

This began English claims to rule Ireland. Norman lords built castles and towns and brought in English settlers, but many became Gaelic in speech and custom. English control often shrank to the area round Dublin called the Pale, until the plantations of the 1600s. It ended the Ireland of Brian Boru.
sum: In 1169 Norman knights from Wales landed in southeast Ireland, invited by Diarmait Mac Murchada, the exiled King of Leinster. Within two years they held Dublin and much of the east.
